description.narrative: Education is a national priority for Moldova in the National Development Strategy (NDS) ‘European Moldova 2030’. Moldova made significant progress on education outcomes over the last decades, but further improvements are needed. Learning losses caused by the pandemic, must be recovered, to avoid the erosion of human capital and long-term damage to Moldovan children's future well-being and productivity. A significant reform of the education system in Moldova relates to embracing a competency-based approach in teaching and evaluation, but more is needed to enhance teachers understanding to practice it in the classroom. Continued efforts are also important to improve equity and inclusion. Despite the progress made, lack of access to preschool education is a persistent challenge for disadvantaged children and younger cohorts. The quality and safety of school infrastructure is an important determinant in educational outcomes, but most public schools are under pressing need of rehabilitation and modernization considering the poor state of existing infrastructure. The Model School initiative of the Government aims to create a more efficient, high-quality and inclusive education system in Moldova in close coordination and cooperation with the development partners and other education stakeholders in the sector. Component 1: Improve quality of teaching. Subcomponent 1.1. Improve quality of teaching practices of participating teachers: this subcomponent will support implementation of in-service training programs for teachers and managers as instructional leaders on revised standards (which include digital pedagogy) prioritizing schools with larger share of disadvantaged students; scale up of assessment of quality of teaching to understand extent that teachers: (a) create a culture that is conducive to learning, (b) instruct in a way that deepens student understanding and encourages critical thinking, (c) foster socioemotional skills that encourage students to succeed both inside and outside the classroom, and (d) use inclusive teaching practices that help all students learn; in-service training for teachers and educators to strengthen pedagogical capacity to implement Early Childhood Education (ECE) Curriculum (ECEC) and support play-based teaching; development of ECE classroom observation tool; quality assessment of sample of ECE service providers. In this sense, the ECEC will also be provided with a standard package which will include the provision of indoor and outdoor teaching and learning and play materials. Subcomponent 1.2. Develop, pilot and implement rapid formative learning assessments in key subject areas (e.g., reading and math) initially in one selected grade to identify lagging students and learning gaps, and to inform instructional practices and tutoring and learning recovery programs targeting disadvantaged students. The Ministry of Education will implement the tutoring program using state budget financing, with technical assistance and support provided by the project. Identification and targeting facilitated by student-level Education Management Information System (EMIS) and other sources of data on vulnerability, socioeconomic status, and academic performance. Subcomponent 1.3. Promote teacher professional development and innovative instructional practices: small grant-supported projects aligned with the NDS “European Moldova 2030” to support: (i) professional development opportunities for teachers and (ii) projects promoting innovative instructional practices in the several priority areas. These include projects relying on: (a) digital tools and focused on active and engaging learning experiences for students; (b) effective student learning assessment and feedback practices used by teachers; (c) active learning, collaborative learning, building a sense of community, belonging and well-being of students; (d) innovative remedial programs for students lagging academically and disadvantaged students including Roma children, refugee students from Ukraine and children with Special Educational Needs (SEN) and disabilities, (e) girls participation in the STEM fields; (f) exchange experiences and mobility programs, creating and developing a community of practice in teaching innovations. They can also support the professional learning network between Moldovan teachers, and potentially collaboration with teachers from Romania, Estonia and other countries facing similar challenges. Component 2: Improve the quality and resilience of learning environments in selected educational institutions. Subcomponent 2.1. Equipping selected schools to improve learning environment. This subcomponent will support (a) an identification study, including the definition of criteria to determine which educational institutions will be selected to receive support (also considering the sustainability of investments in light of declining student population); (b) a needs assessment in each educational institution to determine the availability of basic infrastructure (water supply and sanitation) and put adequate mechanisms in place to ensure local governments supply basic infrastructure, if needed, before receiving investment ; (c) provision of furniture and IT equipment, and STEM equipment for schools, prioritizing energy-efficient equipment to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions; and (d) training of teachers and managers along with user guides and demonstration videos on operating and maintaining IT and STEM equipment as well as the use of such equipment with modern teaching methodologies and digital learning materials in the classrooms. Subcomponent 2.2. Rehabilitation of selected schools and preschools: this subcomponent will support technical preparation and design, civil works, and supervision of civil works. It will focus on school buildings that have the highest risk of collapse or serious damage in an event of an earthquake which could jeopardize the health and safety of students, teachers, and other building users. The project will target/support the schools with lower socioeconomic composition serving a larger share of disadvantaged students. The selection criteria will also prioritize the schools in areas with higher deprivation index, with sufficient school capacity utilization, failing to meet basic WASH and other infrastructure requirements. This will be followed by field verification. Schools on the priority list will be cross-checked to ensure that they are not prioritized under current or future funding by local authorities or other development partners, and that they have not undergone recent comprehensive renovations. This subcomponent would also target ECEC facilities that could expand access (with quality) to the vulnerable children from Moldovan families and refugee children from Ukraine. Minor rehabilitations including WASH facilities in centers that do not have access to water will be supported. Rehabilitation will follow similar prioritization as for schools but will focus only on those ECEC facilities which commit to expand access to vulnerable children from Moldovan families and refugee children from Ukraine, not yet covered by ECEC services. Component 3: Support capacity building for reforms and project management Sub-component 3.1: Capacity building for effective sector and reform management critical sectoral studies and capacity building for policy planning, monitoring and evaluation of reforms and project interventions focusing on support of disadvantaged students; technical assistance, capacity building and critical analytical work to support teacher policy reform including in relation to the use of the artificial intelligence for teaching and learning process in the education sector; PISA and national assessments; rapid assessments of student progress; data management and analytics for evidence-based decision-making, and on ECEC reforms; technical assistance and capacity building on upper secondary education reform; knowle

The objectives of the Project are to: (i) improve the learning environment in participating institutions, with an emphasis on supporting disadvantaged students; and (ii) strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Education and Research for sector management and refugee response.

condition.narrative: The Borrower, through MoER, shall cause NORLD, no later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, to establish and thereaftermaintain throughout Project Implementation, the NORLD's Team, with core staffing, functions, and resources as set forth in theProject Operations Manual.

The Borrower, through MoER, shall no later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, adopt, and thereafter carry out theProject, and cause the Project to be carried out by NORLD, in accordance with the provisions of a manual (the Project OperationsManual) satisfactory to the Bank, which shall include, inter alia: (a) the detailed description of Project activities; (b)institutional arrangements for the oversight, coordination, management, and day-to-day implementation of the Project;(c) functions, responsibilities and composition of the PMT and NORLD's Team; (d) the Project's administrative, accounting,auditing, reporting, financial (including cash flow aspects in relation thereto), procurement and disbursement procedures; (e)arrangements for preventing, detecting, reporting, investigating, remediating and otherwise addressing fraud andcorruption, including compliance with the Anti-Corruption Guidelines; (f) environmental and social management systems, includingthe grievance redress mechanism, gender-based violence and sexual exploitation, and abuse (“GBV/SEA”); and (g) the selectioncriteria for Teachers and Managers, ECE Teachers and Educators, ECEC Service Providers, Priority Areas, Schools, and ParticipatingInstitutions.

The Borrower, through MoER, shall no later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintainthroughout Project implementation, a PMT, with core staffing, functions, and resources as set forth in the Project OperationsManual.

The Borrower, through MoER, shall no later than twelve (12) months after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintainthroughout Project implementation, as applicable, the School Grants Selection Committee, to facilitate the carrying out of Part 1.3of the Project, with core staffing, functions, and resources as set forth in the School Grants Operations Manual.

title.narrative: Parents reporting an improved capacity to work due to ECEC service provision under the project

comment.narrative: The data will be collected and presented following the baseline study.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from improved learning environment under the project (disaggregated by urban/rural, refugee/host community, gender, vulnerability status, education level)

comment.narrative: After the project's interventions on renovations and endowments in educational institutions, indicators will be achieved and reported. Following the completion of the school equipment distribution process, the number of students benefiting from the project's equipment will be estimated in January 2026 and reported.

title.narrative: Participating teachers with improved teaching practices

comment.narrative: A baseline study is currently being carried out to assess the quality of teaching practices in kindergartens. The results are expected to be presented in January 2026.

title.narrative: Number of new high schools constructed in priority areas that meet infrastructure requirements under national quality assurance standards

comment.narrative: Based on cost projections and demographic factors, the MoER has decided not to build the new schools. Instead, through a project restructuring, project funds for this activity will be reallocated for the rehabilitation of 15 beneficiary schools and other related activities of the project.

title.narrative: Number of additional students (disadvantaged/refugee), enrolled in preschool premises renovated and endowed under the project

comment.narrative: Technical design projects for the North, Central, Chisinau, and South areas have been received and are currently under review by the NORLD/EQIP team and, for the North Area, by the World Bank consultant. The procurement process for selecting economic operators to initiate rehabilitation works in the four designated areas will be launched between December 2025 and January 2026, with contract awards anticipated by March–April 2026.

title.narrative: Number of schools renovated under the project that meet infrastructure requirements (national quality assurance standards including on safety, resilience, inclusion, and sustainability requirements)

comment.narrative: The Coordinating Board approved the list of 15 schools to be renovated under the project. Design works for the rehabilitation of 15 schools have already been launchedare being conducted and expected to be received between January and September 2026. Most construction contracts for schools rehabilitations are expected to be awarded June and December 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of students and teachers satisfied with improved classroom learning environment and functionality of schools and preschools under the project

comment.narrative: The percent of school students who are satisfied (satisfied and very satisfied/highly satisfied responses) with teaching and learning environments according to the survey results. The baseline data collection is planned in 2024/25 school year.

title.narrative: Number of direct project host community beneficiaries disaggregated by gender

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of beneficiaries in the communities hosting refugee children from Ukraine and benefiting from project interventions. Initial number of students beneficiaries will be confirmed by the baseline study to be available in February 2026.

title.narrative: Number of direct beneficiaries (refugees) disaggregated by gender

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of refugee children from Ukraine who directly benefit from project interventions disaggregated by gender. The measurement will be conducted following the implementation of relevant interventions. The indicator is expected to be achieved as planned.

title.narrative: Number of sector staff participating in capacity building trainings under the project

comment.narrative: The sector staff engaged in the following capacity-building activities: study visits to model schools for 20 experts; conferences on TEACH and ECEC for 4 experts; training of 9 National Institute for Education Leadership (NIEL) national mentors in TEACH; trainings for 3 PISA national experts; training of 3 experts both in social and environmental management and 3 experts in financial management; 500 teachers trained in providing tutoring program for 9th grade students in mathematics; 275 school coordinators trained for implementation of PISA 2025 evaluation; 105 experts/operators and 460 evaluators/teachers trained in implementing the rapid assessment in mathematics. Two experts in IT attended the event on AI in June 2025.

Currently, 208 teachers and experts were certified as observers in the application of TEACH tool for preschool, primary and secondary levels. Also, as a result of the trainings conducted on the revised professional standards for primary and secondary school teachers, 48 teachers were certified. In addition, 60 certified TEACH observers participated in TEACH training of trainers' program.500 teachers trained in providing tutoring program for 9th grade students in mathematics; 275 school coordinators trained for implementation of PISA 2025 evaluation; 460 evaluators/teachers trained in implementing the rapid assessment in mathematics.

title.narrative: Teachers trained on professional standards under the project (% of teachers in ECEC facilities and grades 1–12)

comment.narrative: The professional standards for teachers were revised and approved by MoER Order no. 1657 dated from 22.09.2025. Consequently, 336 novice teachers from schools were capacitated on revised professional standards. The PMT, in coordination with the MoER, will plan training activities for 2026, with targets that will allow the achievement of the project's indicators.

title.narrative: Targeted schools equipped with school labs, IT equipment, and teaching and learning materials including for students with disabilities

comment.narrative: All planned procurement contracts have been carried out with the selected suppliers. Delivery of goods to the 200 beneficiary schools is currently underway and is expected to be completed by mid-January 2026. Preliminary feedback from school users reveals that the furniture is high-quality, ergonomic, age-adjustable, and features a modern design.

title.narrative: Improved regulatory environment for affordable and quality childcare for preschool children

comment.narrative: To improve the regulatory environment for affordable and quality childcare, the Government approved Decision No. 685 (October 9, 2024) establishing a new standard cost-per-child financing methodology for public pre-primary institutions. The methodology was piloted in four districts (Cahul, Anenii Noi, Nisporeni, Flore?ti) in 2025, and the Ministry of Education and Research (MoER) has since strengthened it to enable nationwide rollout in 2026.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning
Gender gap in STEM education reduced

comment.narrative: Activities related to girls participation in STEM education have been included in SIG Operations Manual.

title.narrative: Annual education statistics reports produced and publicly disseminated based on data generated by the integrated EMIS and used for education sector management including refugee response

target.value: Integrated EMIS is operational and reports, produced using its data, are publicly disseminated and used for education sector management including refugee response.

comment.narrative: Progress towards operationalization of EMIS integration ongoing

title.narrative: Improved learning outcomes of students benefitting from project-supported tutoring program (disaggregated by gender, urban/rural, refugee/vulnerability status)

target.value: Improvement in scores of beneficiaries compared to control group (measured by impact evaluation)

comment.narrative: Analysis of examination results from the first 6000 students who benefited from tutoring program underway. To be finalized in January 2026.

title.narrative: Monitoring tool with reliable gender-disaggregated data to identify disadvantaged students to receive accelerated learning

comment.narrative: Following the approval of the Education Management Information System (EMIS) development priorities by the Bank, a monitoring tool will be developed to provide reliable, gender-disaggregated data for identifying disadvantaged students who require accelerated learning. Based on a national-scale rapid assessment of approximately 30,000 students, the tool will enable the identification of the number of students with learning difficulties, disaggregated by gender. Activities toward achieving this indicator are currently in progress.

title.narrative: Impact evaluations of: (i) tutoring/accelerated learning program and (ii) intervention to accommodate more children in childcare (disadvantaged and refugees)

comment.narrative: The tutoring program was conducted. National Agency for Curriculum Evaluation NACE has prepared a preliminary report on students performance following the tutoring program. 2 experts will support data interpretation and program quality assessment. The Term of Reference (TOR) has been submitted to the Bank for approval, and the report is expected between December 2025 and January 2026. In addition, the TOR for impact assessment of the expansion of Early Childhood Education and Care facilities is in the process of being finalized.

title.narrative: Rapid student assessment mechanism developed and piloted (for selected grade)

comment.narrative: A rapid assessment mechanism was developed and piloted by NACE (covering 9th-grade students in math) between February and March 2025. As a result, 29.894 students participated in this activity. Also, the basic mathematics evaluation for national primary education was conducted in May 13, 2025. Based on the 2025 rapid assessment experience, NACE will adjust the mechanism for evaluating Mathematics and Romanian language in 2026. Also, about 1,700 pupils from 80 educational institutions in 21 districts and municipalities across the country participated digitally. In November 2025, the digital competencies assessment was conducted with 3,200 students (2,200 students in grade 9 and 1,000 in grade 12). The report is expected in December 2025.

title.narrative: Tutoring/accelerated learning program for disadvantaged students developed and implemented (for selected grade)

comment.narrative: The tutoring program for disadvantaged students was carried out in April-May 2025. As a result, 6,000 students (2,293 female and 3,707 male) benefited from the tutoring program.

title.narrative: Percentage of school users who report that consultation processes are effective

comment.narrative: At the first stage, the baseline study will measure school users satisfaction with the consultation process. The indicator is expected to be achieved as planned.
